title: OECD proposes a common reporting framework for AI incidents and hazards
summary: The OECD's AI Incidents Monitor methodology page states that an open submission process following the common reporting framework for AI incidents is being developed to complement incidents and hazards drawn from news articles, and that incidents and hazards in the monitor are already enriched with metadata and criteria from the reporting framework, such as title, summary, country, industry and affected stakeholders. The OECD defines an AI incident as an event where the development, use or malfunction of an AI system directly or indirectly leads to harm, and an AI hazard as an event that could plausibly lead to such an incident.
verification_note: Not verified from the source page. The candidate URL and its oecd.org and doi.org mirrors returned HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge to WebFetch (two attempts) and to curl with browser headers; the Wayback Machine has no snapshot of the URL (availability API empty, /web/2026/ form 404); the web-search budget was exhausted in this run. Existence and current use of the framework were corroborated from the publisher's OECD.AI AI Incidents Monitor methodology page (https://oecd.ai/en/incidents-methodology, fetched 2026-10-17), which links the report and says its criteria already enrich monitor entries, but that page gives no publication date and no criteria count. The February 2025 date is carried over from the sweep candidate with month precision and the day is unconfirmed; the sweep's '29 reporting criteria' figure could not be confirmed and is omitted. The item is about AI systems in general rather than agents specifically; it is kept as relevant because the monitor it feeds already classifies agent incidents and the survey places general AI incident-reporting work in 10.2. A human must open the URL in a browser before publication.
